title: 10 Days in Egypt: A Small-Group Tour of Cairo, the Nile, Luxor and Aswan
excerpt: A 10-day Egypt small-group tour: Cairo and Giza, a four-night Nile cruise from Luxor to Aswan and a Grand Egyptian Museum day. From €1,403 per person, Nov 2026.
body_html:
Prices, timetables and visiting details are a November 2026 snapshot. Check the linked official pages and your departure’s current inclusions and terms before booking.

Quick answer

Ten days is the first length that makes Egypt feel unhurried rather than rushed. This 10-day small-group plan pairs Cairo and Giza with a four-night Nile cruise from Luxor to Aswan, plus one Cairo day you control. The backbone is the Egypt in Depth 9-day Nile cruise and Cairo package on Sawa Tours, from €1,403 per person, as listed in November 2026. Its listing includes both domestic flights, four Cairo hotel nights and four nights on the cruise. The tenth day goes to the Grand Egyptian Museum or another Cairo day tour.

Check current UK government travel advice for Egypt before making your arrangements; advice can change.

Most 10-day Egypt plans fail in one of two directions: they live on a bus, or they see the Nile and skip Cairo. Done in the right order, ten days covers both at a civilised pace, and the logistics are simpler than they look, because one 9-day package carries the hotels, the cruise and both domestic flights. This guide gives you the day-by-day plan, what each stop delivers, the flights-and-trains question and the full cost. It is written by the team behind Sawa Tours (sawa.tours), the Egypt shared-departure platform, founded by an Egyptologist guide who has worked in Egyptian tourism since 1993.

What does a 10-day Egypt small-group tour look like, day by day?

Days 1 to 8 follow the package. The package ends on day 9; instead of flying home that day, you stay one more night in Cairo and use day 9 for the Cairo visit the package does not cover, then fly home on day 10. The extra hotel night is yours to book.

What you'll see at each stop

The route stacks three UNESCO World Heritage areas: Memphis and its Necropolis, ancient Thebes at Luxor and the Nubian monuments. Each stop earns its place by doing something the others cannot.

Cairo and Giza: where the pyramid idea comes from

Day 2 starts at Memphis and Saqqara, and the order is the point. Djoser's Step Pyramid is one of the earliest large stone buildings in the world, and seeing the experiment before the finished article makes Giza legible rather than just photogenic. Old Cairo's Hanging Church and the Coptic quarter then add the two thousand years after the pharaohs. Day 3 pairs the classic Egyptian Museum in Tahrir with the Giza pyramids, Sphinx and Valley Temple.

One change matters here: the Tutankhamun collection has moved from the Tahrir museum to the Grand Egyptian Museum in Giza, so the Tahrir visit in the package no longer includes him. The old museum remains open and still holds the Amarna material and a large general collection, but the Grand Egyptian Museum is a separate visit. That distinction drives the tenth-day choice below.

Luxor: East Bank first, then the West

Karnak's hypostyle hall holds 134 columns, and the avenue of sphinxes, reopened in 2021, once connected the temple to Luxor Temple about 2.7 km to the south. The next day belongs to the West Bank: the Valley of the Kings, best early in the day when the tombs are coolest and emptiest (the general ticket covers three tombs, and a few, such as Tutankhamun's, need an extra ticket that the package does not include), then Hatshepsut's terraces at Deir el-Bahri and the Colossi of Memnon before the boat sails south.

Edfu and Kom Ombo: the temples between the cities

Day 6 is what the cruise is for: the temples come to the boat. Edfu's Temple of Horus is among the best-preserved temples in Egypt, with its great entrance pylon still standing. Kom Ombo is a double temple, dedicated to Sobek and Horus the Elder side by side. Southbound, the boat passes the Esna Lock between Luxor and Edfu, which is one reason sailing times flex.

Aswan and Philae: the river at its calmest

Aswan slows the rhythm on purpose, with time for the souq and the river. Philae, the sanctuary of Isis, sits on Agilkia Island and is reached by motorboat. It was dismantled and rebuilt there in the 1970s, after the Aswan dams left its original island flooded. The High Dam is the modern engineering counterpoint on the same day.

What about Abu Simbel?

Abu Simbel is not on this route. Sawa's packages are fixed products and cannot be extended, so there is no way to add an Aswan night to Egypt in Depth. If Abu Simbel is a must, the 12-day Egypt End to End package includes it, and the Aswan to Abu Simbel day tour (from €50, hotel pickup in Aswan, 3.5 to 4 hours by road each way) suits a trip built around Aswan. For the sun-festival dates, see our guide to the Abu Simbel sun festival.

Getting between Cairo, Luxor and Aswan: flights, trains and what's included

This package includes both domestic flights: its listing includes "Domestic flights Cairo to Luxor and Aswan to Cairo". That matters because the cruise starts in Luxor on day 4, and a self-booked flight is your own connection risk.

Option Time Cost Trade-off
Flight included in the package About an hour to Luxor Inside the package price Arranged around the itinerary; no re-booking risk on your side
Scheduled flight, booked separately About an hour Booked separately You carry the connection risk
Overnight sleeper train (run by Abela Egypt, formerly Watania) About 10 to 11 hours to Luxor, according to Seat 61 Fares quoted in US dollars Saves a hotel night, eats a sightseeing day

If you build the trip yourself, book the Luxor flight with a buffer after any international arrival; the classic DIY mistake is a connection too tight to survive a morning delay. Most travellers also need a visa: check your passport and the current fee on the official portal, visa2egypt.gov.eg.

The day you control: the Grand Egyptian Museum or another Cairo day

The extra day is the plan's pressure valve. The package's Cairo day uses the classic Egyptian Museum, so the Grand Egyptian Museum is a separate visit and deserves its own day. Prices below are per person, as listed in November 2026.

  • Secrets of the Grand Egyptian Museum, from €48. About three hours inside, with general admission included. The lightest option after a busy week.
  • Giza Pyramids, Sphinx and the Grand Egyptian Museum, from €71. About 8 hours, with hotel pickup, lunch and both entry tickets included. Worth it if day 3 at Giza felt rushed. For more on that combination, see Pyramids and the Grand Egyptian Museum in one day.
  • Cairo to Alexandria, from €47. A 10-hour day on the Mediterranean coast, if you would rather see somewhere new.
  • Nile dinner cruise, from €48. A low-energy evening on the river; drinks are extra.

Each day tour is a separate shared departure that needs its own four travellers, so book your flights home only once that date has confirmed, or pick a flight that does not depend on it.

Practical tips for the 10 days

Insider tips from the road

  • Pack for two climates. Cairo evenings can need a jacket in winter, while Aswan at midday is t-shirt weather.
  • Carry small Egyptian pound notes. Tips and site toilets are usually cash.
  • Never book anything time-critical on cruise days. The Esna Lock and river traffic can shift sailing times.
  • Go early at the Valley of the Kings. The site opens at 06:00, and the tombs are coolest and emptiest early in the day.
  • Give the Grand Egyptian Museum its own day. The package's Cairo day is the classic museum; the Grand Egyptian Museum belongs to the extra day, not to a rushed day 3.
  • Sleep in Cairo on your last night. The extra night also protects your flight home from any delay on the domestic flight back from Aswan.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Squeezing the Nile into a three-night cruise to save money: Luxor or Aswan ends up in half-days, and four nights suits this route.
  • Assuming the Grand Egyptian Museum is in the package: the package lists the classic Egyptian Museum.
  • Squeezing Hurghada into the same ten days: that is the job of the 12-day Egypt End to End package (from €1,739 per person, as listed in November 2026).
  • Self-booking domestic flights with no buffer before the cruise starts.
  • Skipping Memphis and Saqqara as a warm-up: it is the day that makes Giza make sense.

The honest downsides, in one place: several early starts, two domestic flights and real midday heat in the warm months. In exchange you get the Nile at cruise pace and Egypt's greatest temple sites from a single cabin for four nights.

How to do the 10-day trip with Sawa

Sawa Tours (sawa.tours) is an Egypt shared-departure platform, operated by Online Era (registration 148500). It runs a fixed catalogue: Sawa sets the calendar and the prices, and travellers booked through several selling agencies share one tour, one date, one guide and one price. The route in this guide is the Egypt in Depth package on Wednesday and Friday dates, from €1,403 per person, as listed in November 2026. On the cruise, your group of up to 8 sails on a shared five-star ship and does the excursions together with its guide.

Here is how a package booking works. Reserving a seat is free and needs no card, and nothing is charged before the GoAhead, the moment four travellers (people, not bookings) have reserved the date. You then pay a 25% deposit, and the balance is due 14 days before departure. A package date has until 30 days before departure to reach four; if it does not, it is cancelled, nothing is charged and Sawa suggests another date. A confirmed date is not cancelled for low numbers. Cancel 30 or more days before departure and there is no charge; from 29 to 15 days before, you lose half the deposit (12.5% of the price); at 14 days or fewer, or if you do not show, the deposit (25%) is retained. Some components, such as flights and cruise cabins, may become non-refundable earlier; if so, that is disclosed before you pay. Force majeure means a full refund. A traveller who does not pay after the GoAhead is excluded, and the tour still runs for everyone else. Groups are never larger than eight. The full rules are in the terms and the GoAhead promise, and the mechanics are explained in how the GoAhead works.

Payments go through a secure payment link from Online Era (General Sales Agent licence 32241); charges are in euros. The departure is operated by one of the licensed Egyptian agencies with travellers on the date, named before the deposit is due. Sawa's founding operating partner is Capital Travel Service (licence 2179). See the forming and confirmed departures, read the FAQ, or message Sawa on WhatsApp at +20 109 284 7613, answered 24/7 while your tour is running.

The short version

Ten days in Egypt works as a fixed shape: three Cairo nights, four nights cruising from Luxor to Aswan, a final Cairo night, and one day you control at the Grand Egyptian Museum. The Egypt in Depth package carries the hotels, the cruise, the guiding and both domestic flights from €1,403 per person; the extra day is the only decision. Nine days is a tour; the tenth is the one that makes it a holiday. Reserve a seat free on a forming departure, or message Sawa on WhatsApp at +20 109 284 7613.

faq.q: What should I do with 10 days in Egypt?
faq.a: Spend three days in Cairo and Giza, four nights on a Nile cruise from Luxor to Aswan, and keep one Cairo day for the Grand Egyptian Museum. That is the 9-day Egypt in Depth package plus one day, and it covers the pyramids, Karnak, the Valley of the Kings and Philae without a rushed transfer. Both domestic flights, Cairo to Luxor and Aswan to Cairo, are listed in the package.

faq.q: Do Egypt tour packages include domestic flights?
faq.a: Some do, and it should be a filter when you compare. The Egypt in Depth package lists "Domestic flights Cairo to Luxor and Aswan to Cairo" among its inclusions; confirm this on the departure page when you book. Packages that exclude flights often look cheaper up front, then add two flight sectors.

faq.q: What does a 10-day Egypt trip cost once international flights are added?
faq.a: The 9-day Egypt in Depth package starts from €1,403 per person, as listed in November 2026, and includes four Cairo hotel nights, the cruise, both domestic flights and 20 meals. On top come your international flights, one extra Cairo hotel night, the tenth-day tour (€48 to €71), drinks, tips and any optional extras such as a Luxor balloon.

faq.q: What happens if the group doesn't fill?
faq.a: Nothing is charged. A shared departure needs four travellers to confirm, the GoAhead. A package date that does not reach four by 30 days before departure is cancelled, nothing is charged and another date is suggested. Once a date confirms, it is not cancelled for low numbers, and groups are never larger than eight. Reserving a seat is free, and the 25% deposit is due only once the date confirms.

faq.q: Can I add Abu Simbel to this package?
faq.a: No. Sawa's packages are fixed products and cannot be extended. If Abu Simbel matters, choose the 12-day Egypt End to End package, which includes it, or plan a separate trip around the Aswan to Abu Simbel day tour (from €50).

faq.q: Egyptian Museum or Grand Egyptian Museum?
faq.a: The package includes the classic Egyptian Museum in Tahrir on day 3; the Grand Egyptian Museum in Giza is a separate visit, and the extra day is the natural slot for it. Tutankhamun's treasures are now at the Grand Egyptian Museum, while Tahrir keeps the Amarna collection and a large general collection, so the two complement each other rather than repeat. If you take only one guided museum, make it the Grand Egyptian Museum.
Sawa's day tours have no solo surcharge. On a package with hotel nights and a cruise, solo rooms and cabins are confirmed in the booking, so check the package page or ask Sawa before you reserve.
